issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, but the reference solution implements these attributes as int. This mismatch between the problem UML and the solution (and the constructor expectations) can confuse students about which types to use and may lead to compile/test failures if tests or instructor expectations assume ints.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement UML to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (matching the solution and typical student counts), or update the solution and template to use double for those attributes. Ensure the constructor and related methods use the same types after the change.

issues.description: The problem instructions (and UML) instruct students to implement a constructor following the UML order and types (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution's constructor uses int parameters for the student counts while the UML lists them as double, creating a constructor-parameter type mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter types with the UML and attributes. Either change the UML and problem text to specify int parameters for the student counts (and update any method signatures accordingly), or modify the solution/template constructor to accept double for the inscribed and guest student parameters. Also update any related methods (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents) to consistently handle the chosen numeric type.
